title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Monthly Rate by the Owner's Standing Across the Books
content:
## Portfolio accounts ruling

The monthly rate at which a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record is charged for instalments left unpaid follows the owner's standing across the company's books and the agreement's own instalment record. Two records are read: what the owner's demand service account under the Demand Service Rate Programs has been invoiced and has paid over the last twelve months, and the instalments invoiced on this agreement against the payments received on it.

### The rule

1. Where the owner's demand service account has been invoiced over the last twelve months and has paid at least as much as it was invoiced, and the instalments invoiced on the agreement exceed the payments received on it by no more than the value of one instalment of the annual price in force, the charge is taken at the rate the office publishes for an owner whose other account is square: **1.0 percent per month**.
2. Where the owner's demand service account has been invoiced over the last twelve months and has paid at least as much as it was invoiced, and the instalments invoiced on the agreement exceed the payments received on it by more than the value of one instalment of the annual price in force, the charge is taken at the rate the office publishes for an owner whose agreement has repeatedly run behind: **1.25 percent per month**.
3. Where the owner's demand service account has not been invoiced at all over the last twelve months, or has been invoiced more over them than it has paid, the charge is taken at the late fee rate the tier publishes.

The value of one instalment of the annual price in force is the annual price in force divided by the tier's instalment count.

### The two records in a table

| Demand service account over the last twelve months | Instalments invoiced less payments received on the agreement | Monthly rate |
|---|---|---|
| invoiced, and paid at least as much as invoiced | no more than the value of one instalment | 1.0 percent per month |
| invoiced, and paid at least as much as invoiced | more than the value of one instalment | 1.25 percent per month |
| never invoiced over those twelve months | any | the late fee rate the tier publishes |
| invoiced, but paid less than invoiced | any | the late fee rate the tier publishes |

### Boundary (hypothetical figures)

An owner whose Demand Service Rate Programs account was invoiced 9 000.00 USD and paid 9 000.00 USD over the last twelve months, on an agreement whose annual price in force is 4 800.00 USD billed in 4 instalments, has an instalment value of 1 200.00 USD. Where the instalments invoiced exceed the payments received by exactly 1 200.00 USD, that is no more than the instalment value, the rate is 1.0 percent per month; where they exceed them by 1 200.01 USD, the rate is 1.25 percent per month.
